# Understanding Brief: Subgroup vote operations

## One-Sentence Test Purpose

This test checks whether Vulkan subgroup vote operations return the required all, any, and all-equal results across active invocations in supported shader stages, including the legacy `VK_EXT_shader_subgroup_vote` forms.

## Background Knowledge

### Subgroup vote scope

A subgroup is an implementation-defined set of shader invocations that can execute collective operations together. Vulkan vote operations compare an expression across the active invocations in that subgroup: all invocations report true, any invocation reports true, or all invocations provide equal values.

Why it matters here:
- Every active invocation receives the collective result, so one incorrect vote can change the per-invocation result mask.
- The active invocation set matters in fragment shaders, where helper invocations participate in shader execution but require separate interpretation.

### Capability and stage support

`VK_SUBGROUP_FEATURE_VOTE_BIT` advertises acceptance of SPIR-V using `GroupNonUniformVote`. Stage support and optional features determine which generated cases may run; required-subgroup-size cases add `VK_EXT_subgroup_size_control` requirements.

Why it matters here:
- Unsupported combinations are rejected before execution rather than treated as failed vote semantics.
- The same operation checks run through compute, graphics, framebuffer, fragment-helper, mesh, and ray-tracing harnesses where supported.

## One Concrete Example

`dEQP-VK.subgroups.vote.compute.subgroupallequal_uint` is generated by `initPrograms`. Its compute shader evaluates five `subgroupAllEqual` conditions and ORs their expected outcomes into `tempRes`. Uniform expressions must compare equal; expressions derived from `gl_SubgroupInvocationID` must compare unequal when the subgroup has multiple invocations. The elected invocation sets the two unequal-result bits as a safeguard for a one-invocation subgroup. A correct invocation writes `0x1F` to its output slot.

## End-to-End Test Flow

```text
[host] select operation, value type, shader stage, and required-subgroup-size variant
[host] reject unsupported vote, format, stage, extension, or subgroup-size combinations
[host] generate the stage program and initialize an input buffer
[host] create descriptors and output storage through the shared subgroup harness
[host] submit the draw, dispatch, mesh, or ray-tracing work
[device] execute several vote expressions and assemble expected-result bits
[device] write one result mask per tested invocation or framebuffer location
[host] read back the result storage
[host] require the expected mask for every checked element; otherwise fail the case
```

## Generated Test Artifacts and Bound Resources

### Generated or loaded program artifacts

The source combines `getStageTestSource` with a shared stage builder. `initPrograms` handles SSBO-backed compute, graphics, mesh, and ray-tracing programs. `initFrameBufferPrograms` handles vertex, tessellation, and geometry framebuffer paths, while `initFrameBufferProgramsFrag` builds the fragment-helper case. Normal and framebuffer paths target SPIR-V 1.3; ray-tracing and applicable mesh paths target SPIR-V 1.4.

### Bound resources and memory objects

| Resource | Created/configured by host? | Bound to GPU? | Read/written by device? | Read back by host? | Why it matters |
|----------|-----------------------------|---------------|-------------------------|--------------------|----------------|
| Input `data` buffer | yes | yes | read | no | Supplies uniform or invocation-indexed values used by the vote expressions. |
| Result SSBO or color attachment | yes | yes | written | yes | Carries the shader's bit mask to the host checker. |
| Specialization constants for local size | yes | yes | read as execution configuration | no | Define compute/mesh local dimensions without changing vote semantics. |

## What Is Checked

- Ordinary vertex-like and compute/mesh paths require every returned value to equal `0x1F`.
- Fragment-helper paths mask the low five vote bits and expect `0x1F` when helper execution was observed, or `0x1E` before it was observed.
- Required-subgroup-size variants repeat the compute or mesh case for each supported power-of-two size from the advertised minimum through maximum.
- Any mismatching checked element fails the test case.

## Behavior Parameter Identification

> **Behavior parameter:** vote operation
>
> **Candidate values:** `subgroupAll` / `allInvocationsARB`, `subgroupAny` / `anyInvocationARB`, `subgroupAllEqual` / `allInvocationsEqualARB`

## What Failure Means

### Failure Cause Mapping

| If this behavior parameter value fails | Possible failure cause(s) |
|----------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| `subgroupAll` / `allInvocationsARB` | Incorrect all-active-invocations reduction, active-invocation handling, or legacy operation lowering. |
| `subgroupAny` / `anyInvocationARB` | Incorrect any-active-invocation reduction, active-invocation handling, or legacy operation lowering. |
| `subgroupAllEqual` / `allInvocationsEqualARB` | Incorrect equality comparison or collective reduction for uniform and nonuniform typed values, including legacy operation lowering. |

Failures shared across operation values can also come from stage-specific result transport, descriptor/input setup, output writes, or host readback rather than the vote operation itself.

## Important Variations and Special Cases

- `subgroupAllEqual` spans the supported scalar and vector types; the other core operations use `uint` predicates.
- Legacy ARB-named operations are nested under `ext_shader_subgroup_vote`, accept scalar boolean arguments, and require `VK_EXT_shader_subgroup_vote`.
- Compute and mesh variants optionally require each supported subgroup size. Graphics, framebuffer, and fragment-helper variants use fixed registration shapes.
- Non-VulkanSC builds add mesh and ray-tracing coverage. Ray-tracing registration covers core operations, not the legacy extension branch.
- Fragment-helper cases deliberately generate derivatives and record whether a helper invocation participated, changing the host's expected low-bit mask.
